en: A long, endless conflict, the\norigins of which are lost to\ntime.

A flame that sometimes
smolders and sometimes
blazes between the two great
powers of the Schenberyl
continent: the Kingdom of
Rubarika and the Baschen
Empire.

Clashing over the "Holy Land of
Asyl," these two nations have
sent thousands upon
thousands of their people to
the front lines of the Holy Land
War throughout history.

The nations, the people, and
the land itself were exhausted
to their limits by the war that
spanned countless ages.
Yet, the fighting could not\nstop; it would not stop.

For if they ceased, if they
retreated, the enemy―who had
fought this timeless struggle
alongside them―would seize an
overwhelming power.
The "Messenger of Daftes."
That overwhelming power is\nbrought by a being known by\nthat name.

Whoever triumphs in the Holy
Land War and claims the Holy
Land of Asyl earns the honor
of welcoming the "Messenger
of Daftes," who descends via
the "Ladder of Moonshadow."

Throughout the long history of
conflict, the "Messenger of
Daftes" has bestowed various
blessings, powers, and wisdom
beyond human comprehension
upon both Rubarika and
Baschen.

To welcome as many
"Messengers of Daftes" as
possible became the ultimate
mandate and the sole purpose
of both Rubarika and Baschen.

So, yeah, that's the gist of the
Holy Land War that <font color=yellow>Rubarika</font>
and <font color=yellow>Baschen</font> have been
fighting for all these years.

Huh... Since you called it a
"Holy Land," I thought it was
some kind of religious war, but
it's more about practical gains
than I expected.

You really didn't know? I
thought even the small
neighboring countries were
aware of it.

U-uh, well, we don't stay in one
place for very long, so we don't
really get many chances to
hear about history and things
like that!
Hmm.

Both Rubarika and Baschen
have plenty of heroic tales and
legends about the Holy Land
War, but you don't use those
for your performances?

W-war stories are usually so
sad, right?! Our whole selling
point is being relentlessly
cheerful! Ahahaha...
Ah... well, that makes sense. I\nguess that's a valid reason.
(She's being backed into a\ncorner by her own lie.)
(Yeah... Eve is sweating a lot.)

Anyway, that Holy Land War is
intensifying right now. That's
why... the public safety has
deteriorated like this.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Phew... You guys really
are strong. Those weapons and
gadgets aren't just for show,
are they?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> You shouldn't be so\nsurprised.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> No, I am surprised. Put
bluntly, I'm surprised that you
possess such things. They
aren't the kind of items that
usually circulate in the world.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> What do you mean by\nthat?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I mentioned it earlier.\nThe story of the <font color=yellow>Messenger of\nDaftes</font>.

Among the <font color=yellow>Messenger's
powers</font> obtained by the victors
of the Holy War, there is
something very similar to what
you have, Verda.
The same goes for Tika's\nmechanical arm.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> What does that mean?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Exactly what it sounds\nlike... It's essentially a blessing\nfrom the gods.

The Messenger of Daftes
provides things that could
never be created using the
powers Rubarika or Baschen
possess.

<font color=blue>Eve</font> I don't quite understand,
but... I can see why people
would go to war to obtain such
power.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Then is your power also\na "Messenger's power," Euwin?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Huh? Oh, this? Uh... no,\nthis is different.
This... well, someone gave it to\nme.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I see...

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Anyway, because of that
Holy War, bandits and
"Baschen's Beasts" are roaming
everywhere, and law and order
have completely collapsed.
Big brother Euwin, why were\nyou in Dagris?

Ah, it's because the people of
Dagris petitioned for someone
to do something about the
security around their village.
Now that you mention it, the\nvillage kids did say something\nabout that.
But would the son of a lord\nreally be dispatched alone for\nsuch a thing?
He wouldn't. Of course not.
...What do you mean?

When the villagers of Dagris
came to petition, I happened to
be called back to my family
home.

Having traveled far and wide
and seen the damage caused
by the beasts of Baschen, I
told them that the petition
should be granted.

But my father, the current lord,
and my eldest brother, the
heir, just laughed it off. They
said Carlone doesn't have the
luxury for that right now.
...Even though they're sending\nmountains of soldiers to the\nfront lines of the Holy War.
Big brother Euwin...
I happened to be fed up with\nmy brother's lecturing at the\ntime, too, so...

My father and brother wouldn't
stop nagging me to behave in a
way that wouldn't bring shame
to the Rakstar name.

So, I came here to do
something worthy of a member
of the Rakstar family. That's
all.
...The concept of Noblesse\nOblige, then.
Noble... what?

Noblesse Oblige is a term that
symbolically represents the
ethical norm that those with
privilege are recognized by
fulfilling their obligations to
those without.
It is a standard of moral\nresponsibility.
Hmm. I don't really get it, but\nBrother Euwin is amazing!

It's not like that. I'm just doing
this as part of my adventure.
Just testing my skills... testing
my skills...
Wait, did I just hear a weird\nvoice...?

Aaaaah!! But still! The Village
Chief was so grateful when you
left! You don't have to be so
shy and call it "testing your
skills"!
What's wrong?
I'm not being shy; I'm genuinely\nembarrassed!
Huh?
Rubarika holds a significant\nadvantage in the current Holy\nGround War.

That's why every noble house
is racing to send personnel to
the front lines, hoping for
post-war rewards or the
"Power of the Messenger."
As a result, none of the\nterritories can properly\nmaintain public order.

They're leaving bandits like
those from before, and "Beasts
of Baschen" crossing the
border, to run wild.

And yet, the Rakstar family
won't even bother to protect a
single village in their own
territory. A noble is nothing
without their people.

My father and brothers just
laughed it off, not even
stopping the outcast fifth son
from playing the hero under
the guise of a village
inspection.

As a member of the Rakstar
family, it's embarrassing that
I'm the only one who has to go
and protect the village.
...Quite the remarkable young\nman.

...I suppose. Though he has the
kind of personality that usually
ends up getting the short end
of the stick.

Please don't. I know. Thanks to
that, I'm perpetually broke. I'm
not at an age or in a position
to get an allowance from my
family.
Which is why I'm really counting\non the reward.
Now then, the road from here\nto Carlone is quite a trek. Let's\nstay sharp.
Right... It seems you're carrying\na heavy burden too, Euwin.
Which means he likely knows a\ngreat deal. We shall be relying\non you.
Tika's safety is the top priority.\nI hope you do not forget that.
Rekoro, I'll be fine.

We know, we know. We've
taken that to heart. We
wouldn't dream of getting our
priorities mixed up.
I hope we can uncover more\nanswers as we go.
For now, let's follow Euwin.\nFirst, we have to make it to\nCarlone!
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Phew... Even though we\nsaid we came from Dagris, that\ncheckpoint was awfully intense.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Indeed. If we didn't have
Euwin's Rakstar family crest, I
can't imagine what kind of
unreasonable demands they
would have made.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Those soldiers were\nscary...

<font color=blue>Eve</font> The Captain is right.
Because of the war, even the
soldiers in the interior are on
edge. It might be related to the
rumors that public order is
deteriorating.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> But they didn't say\nanything about Verda's gun or\nmy Arms.
Maybe it's because everyone\nknows about the "Power of the\nEnvoy."

<font color=blue>Eve</font> There are so many things
that don't sit right with me... I'm
feeling uneasy, so I hope Euwin
comes back soon.
He disappeared somewhere as\nsoon as the checkpoint was\nover; I wonder what happened.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> He said he was going
ahead to arrange the travel
permits to leave the city, but I
wonder if he ran into some
trouble...
Ah, thank goodness. Speak of\nthe devil.
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Hey, sorry to keep you\nwaiting. ...Things got a bit\ncomplicated, so I'm late.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Complicated how?
<font color=blue>Euwin</font> The eastern highway to\nthe royal capital has been\nclosed.

Apparently, a large number of
"Baschen's Beasts" have
appeared, and travel is
prohibited for a while to carry
out a sweep operation.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Is there no other way to\nthe royal capital?

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> There are, but I wouldn't
recommend them. You're
already people of uncertain
origin.

Posing as traveling performers
during wartime is practically
asking to be suspected of
being spies.

Rakstar's name carries weight
in some places, but not others.
Unless every second counts,
it's better to wait here.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I suppose so. Though\nconsidering Tika, we can't\nafford to dawdle too long.
Would it be acceptable if we\nwere the ones to exterminate\nthose beasts?

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> Now, now, don't be
unreasonable. The knights
guarding the city walls and
highways have taken heavy
losses.

I know you're strong, but as
your guide, I can't let you
throw yourselves into danger.
Please, just be patient.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> This is a problem.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Big brother Euwin is using\nhis name to help us out, so we\nshouldn't push him too hard.
I'll be fine, so why don't we wait\na little longer?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> ...Hmm, it seems we\nwere being rather impatient.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> ...You're right. Sorry, Euwin.

<font color=blue>Euwin</font> I appreciate you
understanding. I'm going to go
check on the state of the town
a bit more.
I've already arranged an inn, so\nif you want to rest, please go\nto the one on this note.

Also, you're free to explore the
town, but please try not to do
anything that draws too much
attention.
For now, let's meet back at the\ninn for dinner. See you then.

Hmm... such hospitality. It
would be best if I avoided
doing anything to
inconvenience Euwin.
You're right. Let's just be\npatient and wait for the\nlockdown to be lifted.
What do you think, Captain?\nWant to take a stroll through\ntown?
Looks like this is the North\nGate. That means we can go\nwest, east, or south?
Let's head west.
Let's head south.
Let's head east.
Let's go back to the North\nGate.
Let's rest at the inn for today.
It looks like the west side is\nwhere the wealthy live.
There are so many soldiers.
From what I can see, none of\nthe soldiers have anything like\nVerda's gun or Tika's Arms.
Rekoro, do you detect anything\nthat doesn't match the\ncivilization level of this planet?

Within scanning range, I cannot
detect any devices or gadgets
that defy the current
civilization level.

I see. Euwin mentioned they
were rare, so maybe only
high-ranking military officers
have them.

Look over there. That flag has
the same emblem Euwin
showed us at the city wall
checkpoint. That's probably the
estate of the Rakstar family,
the lords of Carlone.
We'll likely be suspected if we\nget any closer. Best we make\nour exit.
This was the west side, right?\nWhere to next?
It seems the south is the\nindustrial center of the city.
There are so many shops!
But it's not very lively. I don't\nsee anyone shopping at all.

Perhaps it is because of the
war, or maybe the roads to the
royal capital are blocked and
goods aren't arriving. Either
way, it doesn't seem like a
good time for a leisurely
shopping trip.
Huh? Isn't that Euwin over\nthere?
You're right. I wonder what he's\ndoing in front of that closed\nshop.
Perhaps there was something\nhe wanted to buy, but it\nhappened to be their day off.
Oh, he's gone. I wonder what\nkind of shop it was.

A sign with a drawing of a
hand with the index finger
raised... I can't tell what they
sold.

There is no need to force
ourselves to gather materials
or resources right now, so it
seems there is nothing for us
to do here. Shall we explore
elsewhere?
This was the south side, right?\nWhere to next?
The east seems to be a\nresidential area.
But it's already evening, and so\nfew houses have their lights\non.

You're right. There's no smoke
coming from the chimneys
either... I wonder if anyone
even lives here.

The balance between the
number of biological heat
sources and the number of
dwellings is extremely poor.

I infer that there are a
considerable number of vacant
houses once you move from
the main street into the back
alleys.
I wonder what that means.

Even in dwellings where
biological heat sources are
present, many show no
detectable heat sources from
fuel.
I speculate that the shortage\nof supplies caused by the road\nblockade is hindering daily life.

I wonder if the blockade has
been going on for a long time.
If we could solve it, I'd love to
help them...
Euwin told us not to, so we\ncan't cause any trouble.

Come to think of it, he
mentioned that the gate
leading to the road to the royal
capital is on this east side.
Huh? I feel like I just saw\nEuwin... or maybe I'm just\nimagining things.
In any case, it seems there is\nnothing for us to gain here.
We don't want to carelessly\ntalk to the guards and make\nthem suspicious of us, either.
This was the east side, right?\nWhere to next?
The North Gate closes by\nevening.
I wonder if the people of Dagris\nare okay.
I overheard earlier that a\nsecurity force has been\ndispatched.
Really! That's a relief!

It seems the road to the royal
capital in the east being
blocked is a big reason for it. If
the "Beasts" ravaged the north
side too, the town would be
completely isolated.
So they've finally gotten\naround to doing something. A\nblessing in disguise, I suppose.
Still, I wonder what the "Beast\nof Baschen" actually is.

I wonder if it's related to the
stories about there being lots
of "Beasts" on the eastern
highway near Dagris.
It may not be unrelated...\nthough there is no way for us\nto verify that right now.

Regardless, the safety of the
people of Dagris has been
secured, so we'll just have to
be satisfied with that for now.
It's getting late. Shall we move\non?
This is the North Gate, right?\nWhere to next?
Right, let's head to the inn\nEuwin arranged for us.
This inn is far more luxurious\nthan I expected.
The bed is so fluffy!
We really owe Euwin a lot. I feel\nlike all the fatigue from our\njourney is just melting away.
Tika, are you feeling alright?
Yeah! I'm fine! Right, Rekoro?

Affirmative. While there is a
slight decrease in physical
stamina, no major abnormalities
are detected.
If Tika is okay, then let's have\na brief strategy meeting before\nEuwin returns.

<font color=blue>Eve</font> You're right. I am curious
to see what the town of
Carlone looks like from space.
Coro?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "..."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro?

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...Since nobody really
talks to me, I just figured you'd
all forgotten about me. What is
it, Miss Eve?"
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Stop sulking. How\nchildish.
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Exactly. There's no way I\ncould talk to you while Euwin is\naround.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Hmph! Hmph!"

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Captain. It appears
your ship's AI, Coro, exhibits
excessive emotional expression
unnecessary for stable ship
operation. I must suggest that
this could become an obstacle
to Tika's safety.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Hmph!! Fine by me! I'm
just a useless AI whose only
merit is being creepy-cute
anyway!"
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Coro... I'm sorry. Were you\nlonely?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...Hmph."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro! Cheer up already!\nTika is actually apologizing to\nyou!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "...So, what was it you\nwanted again?"

<font color=blue>Eve</font> Honestly! I want to know if
the long-range sensors in
space have picked up anything
strange in Carlone City!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Nothing in particular~"
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Coro! Take this seriously!

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I am being serious! I
really can't detect anything
from Carlone City that doesn't
match the average civilization
level of this planet!"

At least I haven't detected
anything like the 'servants of
Daftes' or 'servant powers'
that Euwin mentioned!
<font color=blue>Eve</font> ...I see.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> What about the "Beast\nof Baschen"? Which is to say,\nthe Thornite.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "That's the thing. On the
road toward the royal capital
that Euwin mentioned, I can't
detect any biological
signatures of the size or
number that would cause that
much damage to the knights."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> What does that mean?
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I can pick up the\nsubjugation force that was\ndispatched from Carlone.

There's a large forest along
the road, and I suspect the
pack of beasts is in there, but
I can't find any signatures that
look like beasts anywhere."
<font color=blue>Eve</font> It's not interference again,\nis it? Not that there's a Pulse\nTower around here.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "I don't think that's the\ncase, but...

To begin with, I can't
distinguish between a
Thornite-mutated individual and
a normal one without optical
confirmation, so honestly, I
can't tell what's actually
happening on the ground."
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Hmm. Perhaps we will\nknow more once Euwin returns.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> "About that... don't you
think it'd be faster to just warp
straight to the royal capital of
Rubarika instead of waiting for
the blockade to be lifted?"
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That's true, but Euwin's\nguidance is invaluable.
Going to the royal capital\nblindly is completely different\nfrom going while being guided.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> Indeed. Even in this
town, the unsettling effects of
the war are visible everywhere.
There is no guarantee that the
royal capital is any safer.

With Euwin as our guide, we
can at least reduce the risk of
being treated as suspicious
persons.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Tika.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Yes?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Do you know anything\nabout the Holy War?
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Not more than what Big\nBrother Euwin already told me...

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> I presume that at Tika's
age, she would not have had
the opportunity to learn the
details.

This vessel also has no
recorded data that could
update the basic information
regarding Ewin Laxter.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> I'm sorry...
<font color=blue>Eve</font> Don't apologize. It's not\nyour fault, Tika.
From now on, if you notice\nanything or feel even a little\nuneasy, you must tell us, okay?
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Okay...

<font color=blue>Eve</font> Anyway, we'll follow Euwin's
lead tomorrow and head for
the capital of Rubarika as soon
as the road blockade is lifted.
Does that sound right?

Coro, you're not to make a
sound unless it's absolutely
necessary. Euwin will get
suspicious!
<font color=blue>Verda</font> I wonder if Coro is even\ncapable of such a feat.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "That's easy! If worst\ncomes to worst, I'll just say the\nCaptain is doing ventriloquism!"

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> Captain. I advise you to
be wary of the behavioral
algorithm of your ship's AI,
Coro, which causes him to sulk
if not spoken to regularly.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Rekoro! Saying things like\nthat is exactly what makes me\nsulk!"
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Ah, it looks like Euwin is\nback. We'll continue this later.
<font color=blue>Coro</font> "Geez...!"
Sorry I'm late. ...Was there\nanyone else in this room just\nnow?
What!? N-no one was here!
I see... I thought I heard a\nvoice...
Well, never mind. Phew, maybe\nI'm just a bit tired.
Are you okay, Big Brother\nEuwin?
Yeah, sorry. Don't worry about\nme...

About the blockade on the
eastern road―it looks like it
won't be lifted for a while.
Apparently, they're struggling
with the subjugation.
So, it looks like you'll have to\nstay in this town for a bit.
I see. It cannot be helped.
Carlone isn't a bad town. I hope\nyou enjoy your stay. Well then,\nI'm going to bed...
O-oh, okay.
He seemed strangely rushed.

I see. Captain, you're sharing a
room with Euwin, right? Well, if
he seems unwell, please keep
an eye on him.
...Big brother Euwin...
Huh?
Captain. Do you need\nsomething from Rekoro?
...Right. She's asleep.
Sorry. I'll be back as soon as I\ncan.
I have to hurry...!
Where are you going?
?! Tika!
...Are you going to fight the\n"beasts" on the road by\nyourself?
...Ugh... Well, this is bad. I didn't\nthink you'd notice...
You told me not to just now.

Circumstances have changed.
It seems a rather hot-headed
friend of mine is about to do
something reckless.
A friend?
One of the few friends I can\ntruly open up to.
An eccentric fellow who made\nthis weapon for me.
In that case, maybe Eve and\nthe others could come along...

This is a personal matter of
mine. I can't involve you all in
something dangerous. Not even
as guides.

I'll be back by morning, without
fail. I promise I won't do
anything reckless. So, please
just wait for me without saying
a word...
Though, I have a feeling you\nwon't listen.
...Ehehe.
Which is why I'll be blunt. It's\nuseless to wake the others. I\nam a citizen of Rakstar.

I can pass through the
checkpoints in the middle of
the night without a problem,
but you all couldn't get
through, even with me.
Big brother Euwin...
Hehe. You're all too kind. I have\nto put it this way for you to\ngive up. Well then, I'm off.
Rekoro.

No problem. Per the captain's
orders, I already hid a
transmitter in Ewin Laxter's
clothing during dinner. Tracking
him will be easy.
The Captain was awake.
...Yeah! I got it.
Big sister Eve! Big sister Verda!\nCoro! Wake up!
*Pant... pant...* That idiot... just\nhow far did he wander in...?

The people at the camp said
they haven't seen him, and for
that matter, how can we not
even know where the beast
packs are...?
Damn... that was close.
Strange... these are far\nstronger than the ones near\nDagris.
I hope he's alright... I told him\nto at least wait until I got back!
...! Over there?!
What?! W-when did it get\nhere?! Where did something\nthis huge even come from!
Whoa!?
Damn it! It's huge, but it's fast!\nAt this rate...!
Summon Comet!!
Euwin! Are you alright!
Big brother! Are you hurt!?
Y-you guys, what are you doing\nhere!?
We'll talk later! Right now,\ndealing with this swarm of\nThornite comes first!
R-right!
We managed to take it down.
...You really saved me. I\nwould've been finished if I were\non my own. Thank you.
Before that, don't you have\nsomething to say to Tika and\nthe rest of us?
Big brother Euwin...!
...Yeah. I'm sorry for leaving\nwithout a word. And for trying\nto keep it a secret.

Big brother Euwin and I are
friends now. So... if you're
having trouble, I want you to
tell me.
Even if there isn't much I can\ndo to help.
...Friends, huh. It feels strange.\nI've had very few of those in\nmy life.
Exactly. This kind of thing isn't\nabout how much time you've\nspent together!
I'm just glad you're safe, big\nbrother Euwin. Let's hurry and\nsave our other friends!
Right. Thank you. I look forward\nto working with you.

But how on earth did you all
get past the checkpoint?
Security should be especially
tight at this hour...

Hmm? Well, let's just say that
even the gates of hell open for
a one-way ticket if you know
the right people.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> I've been waiting, Captain.
I've already traced Euwin's
coordinates. He's moving
deeper and deeper into the
forest.

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> A landing point
approximately one hundred
meters away from Ewin Laxter
is deemed optimal.

<font color=blue>Coro</font> I agree. Carlone's
subjugation force has
surrounded the forest, but
they haven't ventured deep
inside.

Until morning, the light from a
teleportation beam within a
hundred-meter radius of Euwin
should go unnoticed.
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Do you know where\nEuwin's friends are?

<font color=blue>Coro</font> It's a forested area with
poor visibility, and it's difficult
to track local residents who
aren't tagged. We don't even
know who they are...
<font color=blue>Eve</font> That means we'll just have\nto go down there and save\nthem ourselves!
<font color=blue>Tika</font> Let's go, hurry!
<font color=blue>Coro</font> Just to be sure, Rekoro,\nis it really okay to let Tika drop\ndown?

<font color=blue>Rekoro</font> As a life-pod AI, I have
reservations about deploying
Tika into an area with a high
probability of combat.

However, if Ewin Laxter is lost,
the objective of Tika returning
